sections.html:
Barnstable is the county seat of Barnstable County and the largest community on Cape Cod by land area and population, roughly 70 miles southeast of Boston. Cape Cod Bay forms its northern edge and Nantucket Sound its southern edge.

The town is a group of villages with no legal boundaries of their own. These seven are the ones most often listed:

  • Barnstable village, which includes Cummaquid
  • Centerville
  • Cotuit
  • Hyannis, which includes Hyannis Port and West Hyannisport
  • Marstons Mills
  • Osterville
  • West Barnstable

Most residents live in the south, many near the beaches of Centerville and Hyannis Harbors. Hyannis, the biggest village, is the commercial center of the Cape, with Cape Cod Hospital, Barnstable Municipal Airport and the ferries to Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard. Route 6 runs across town as a four lane freeway, and the nearest year-round commuter rail is at Middleborough and Kingston, so a commute to Boston is mostly a drive.

Barnstable swapped selectmen and town meeting for a council and town manager in 1989. Thirteen Massachusetts municipalities have a city government but keep "the town of" in the name, and Barnstable is among them. For paperwork, go to Town Hall at 367 Main Street in Hyannis.

Roughly 30 inches of snow falls from November through April, with February the worst and nor'easters at their peak. Inspectors for buyers tend to start with the roof and heating.

With a cash buyer those repairs are optional. Storm damage to a roof or deck does not block a sale.

Real estate tax comes in four quarterly payments per fiscal year. Preliminary bills one and two come due in early August and early November. Bills three and four are actual bills, due on these fiscal 2027 dates:

BillDue date
Third quarter (actual bill)February 1, 2027
Fourth quarter (actual bill)May 3, 2027

The actual bills are to be mailed by December 31, 2026. The Collector bills other items too: motor vehicle and boat excise, sewer usage, and betterments for roads, water, sewer and septic. A betterment attaches to the property, so tell your closing attorney about any you know of.

A municipal lien certificate request form is on the Collector's page, and your attorney can say if your sale needs one. Tax Collections answers at 508-862-4054.

A value that looks too high calls for an abatement application to the assessors. Quarterly-billing towns generally set the cutoff at February 1, and appeals then go to the Appellate Tax Board. Keep paying installments while the request is open.

A house on septic usually needs an inspection when it sells. State Title 5 rules call for one in the two years before the sale, or in the six months after if weather got in the way. Barnstable bills for sewer and for septic betterments, so some addresses are on sewer and some are not. Find out which applies to yours.

  • The inspector must be MassDEP approved, and the report is filed on the state form within 30 days.
  • Give the buyer a copy of the report.
  • A pass lasts two years in general, or three if the system is pumped every year and the records are in the report.
  • A conditional pass can cover a cracked tank or broken pipe. Cesspools and soil absorption systems cannot be fixed that way.
  • A failed system has to be upgraded within two years unless the Board of Health sets another schedule.

Transfers among spouses, parents and children, or full siblings are exempt, along with some trust and estate planning transfers. A buyer can also sign a binding agreement with the Board of Health to upgrade or tie into sewer within two years.

The state taxes a deed when it is recorded. For Barnstable County the statute's rate is below the one for the rest of the state: $1.50 per $500 of consideration or fraction of it. The registry sets recording fees on its own schedule, so your closing attorney can tell you what applies.

Plan for three things when you sell a one or two family home.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. The fire department issues a certificate of compliance once your alarms pass. Phone it when a closing date is set, and expect a fee. Battery alarms past ten years get replaced with sealed ten year photoelectric units.
  • An attorney. Closings here count as legal work, so hire one early.
  • Title system. Most land is recorded at the Registry of Deeds. Some parcels are registered land, which carries a Land Court certificate of title.

One more rule: for certain residential properties, a seller cannot make an offer depend on the buyer waiving a home inspection.

Cape houses often carry charges that a mainland seller never sees. A betterment is a charge for roads, water, sewer or septic work, and it stays with the property. Sewer usage is billed separately from the tax bill. Before you list, ask the Collector whether any betterment is open and whether it will be paid off at closing or passed to the buyer.

Vacant seasonal houses add another wrinkle. A house that sat empty through a Cape winter may have roof, heating or plumbing damage, and it may have an old septic system nobody has inspected. Get the inspection scheduled early, since a failed system can reshape the whole sale, and a buyer who plans to upgrade must sign an agreement with the Board of Health.

Write down what you learn from each office, with dates, and give the list to your attorney. It saves a round of phone calls at the end.

1. Call the Collector at 508-862-4054 for your balance and any betterment on the property.
  2. Find out whether the house is on sewer or septic. If septic, line up an approved inspector.
  3. Choose a closing attorney and share the tax and betterment details.
  4. Schedule the fire department alarm certificate as soon as a date is set.
  5. At closing the deed is recorded, the excise tax is paid, and any tax balance comes out of your proceeds.

Selling as-is to Cash Home Buyers keeps repairs off the list, but the septic report, the alarm certificate and the tax payoff still apply. Ask us how each one will be handled when you request an offer.

Seven villages mean seven different settings, from harbor streets in Hyannis to the wooded interior near Wequaquet Lake. A house in Cotuit and a house in West Barnstable can have very different sewer, water and tax situations, so confirm the details with the Collector and the Board of Health instead of assuming.

If the house needs septic work, carries a betterment, or sat vacant through a Cape winter, a direct sale can spare you the repair bills and the wait for an inspector. Cash Home Buyers buys Barnstable houses as they are.

faqs.q: Is Barnstable a town or city?
faqs.a: It is both. The name stays Town of Barnstable, but a council and town manager charter has governed since 1989.

faqs.q: How many villages are in Barnstable?
faqs.a: Seven are commonly listed: Barnstable, Centerville, Cotuit, Hyannis, Marstons Mills, Osterville and West Barnstable. They have no legal boundaries.

faqs.q: When is the next Barnstable property tax payment due?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027 the remaining dates are February 1, 2027 for the third quarter and May 3, 2027 for the fourth. Check your actual bill, since the Collector sets the schedule each year.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic inspection to sell my Barnstable house?
faqs.a: Normally, if the house has a septic system. Title 5 requires it, with limited exemptions such as family transfers. Timing is within two years before the sale or six months after if weather blocks it.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Barnstable County?
faqs.a: $1.50 per $500 of the price or fraction of it. Your closing attorney can work out the amount for your sale.
